response.title: Harborlight FY2026 Results and FY2027 Request

segments.heading: Who we served
segments.text: In fiscal year 2026, Harborlight reached more adult learners than the year before. Now staff ask the board to pay for a sixth site. Here is a look at who came to learn. Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners at five neighborhood sites. The year before, it enrolled 936. Of these learners, 412 worked toward a high school equivalency credential. Another 389 were English language learners.

segments.heading: Results and people
segments.text: Some learners stayed at least 12 weeks. Sixty-eight percent of them gained one or more reading levels on the CASAS assessment. Seventy-one learners earned a high school equivalency credential. No year in Harborlight's history has seen more. A group of 214 volunteer tutors gave 9,870 tutoring hours. On average, a tutor stayed 14 months. Harborlight has 11 full-time staff, and four of them are site coordinators. One learner at the Riverside site said, "I read my granddaughter a bedtime story for the first time this spring."

segments.heading: The money
segments.text: Harborlight spent $1,420,000 to operate in fiscal year 2026. Programs took 81 percent of that spending. Foundation grants brought in $640,000. Individual donors gave $388,000. The city's adult education contract paid $295,000. Each learner cost $1,237 to serve. There is one warning sign. The treasurer reported that reserves stand at 3.2 months of operating expenses. The board's target is 4 months, so reserves fall short.

segments.heading: The waitlist
segments.text: Here is the problem in plain terms. More adults want to learn than Harborlight has room for. At the end of the year, 287 adults sat on the waitlist. Most of them were waiting for the Eastgate and Riverside sites. On average, they waited nine weeks. This gap between demand and space is the reason behind the staff request.

segments.heading: What staff ask for
segments.text: Staff ask the board to approve an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000. The budget pays for a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library. It also pays for two more site coordinators. Staff think the sixth site would serve 180 more learners a year. They also think it would cut the waitlist in half. At the September 13 retreat, the board asked staff for a one-page budget summary for the October 21 meeting. Board members also wanted a short deck to share with funders. The board agreed to vote on the budget on October 21.

response.recap: Keep three points in mind. First, Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners, and seventy-one earned a high school equivalency credential, a record. Second, 287 adults sat on the waitlist, and reserves stand at 3.2 months, short of the 4-month target. Third, staff ask for an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000 to open a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library.
